sources.title: Apollo 11 Lunar Module / EASEP: the descent stage served as a platform for launching the ascent stage and was left behind on the Moon; EASEP with a passive seismometer and the laser retroreflector were deployed
Apollo 11 Plaque: "Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the moon, July 1969 A.D. We came in peace for all mankind." Attached to the ladder on the landing-gear strut of the descent stage

Apollo 11 Mission Overview, mission highlights: launch 16 July 1969, 9:32 a.m. EDT, Launch Pad 39A, Saturn V; Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins, Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin; lunar orbit insertion at about 75 h 50 min (July 19); Eagle undocked from Columbia; landed in the Sea of Tranquility, partly flown by hand by Armstrong to avoid a crater; 'one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind'; plaque attached to the descent stage; solar wind composition experiment, seismic experiment package and Laser Ranging Retroreflector; the EVA lasted more than two and a half hours; ascent stage fired after a rest period; docked with Columbia; splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on 24 July

Apollo 11 Lunar Module / EASEP (NSSDCA 1969-059C): landed 20 July 1969, 20:17:40 UT; Armstrong reporting "Houston, Tranquility Base here - the Eagle has landed"; they set up a flag, deployed the EASEP, took photographs and collected 21.55 kg of lunar rock and soil, including two core tube samples

Apollo 11 (NSSDCA): launched 16 July 1969, 09:32:00 a.m. EDT; landed on the Moon 20 July 1969, 20:17:40 UT, Sea of Tranquility; returned to Earth 24 July 1969; Armstrong commander, Collins command module pilot, Aldrin lunar module pilot
Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: Apollo 11 landing transcript, 102:45:58: "Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed."
sources.publisher: NASA History Office (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal)
